cues.zh: 这个国家最畅销的经济学教科书出自 N. Gregory Mankiw 之手。
cues.en: Great, so the best-selling economics textbook in the country is by N. Gregory Mankiw.

cues.zh: 它就建立在这十大经济学原理之上。
cues.en: It's based on these 10 Principles of Economics.

cues.zh: 就是这些。我不打算给你们念，你们就信我一句：得有个经济学博士学位才看得懂。
cues.en: Here they are. I'm not going to read them for you, just take my word for it that you need a PhD in economics to understand these.

cues.zh: 幸好我有一个……于是我就自告奋勇，替还没入门的人翻译一下这些原理。
cues.en: Fortunately I have one... and I have taken it upon myself to translate these principles for the uninitiated.

cues.zh: 先分成两部分：前七条是微观经济学，后三条是宏观经济学……
cues.en: Let's begin by separating them into the first seven principles, which are microeconomics, and the last three, which are macroeconomics...

cues.zh: 区别当然在于，微观经济学家是在具体的事情上出错……
cues.en: the difference of course being that microeconomists are people who are wrong about specific things...

cues.zh: ……而宏观经济学家是在一般性的事情上出错。[这是对 P.J. O'Rourke 的转述。]
cues.en: ...and macroeconomists are wrong about things in general. [This is a paraphrase of P.J. O'Rourke.]

cues.zh: 宏观经济学的所有原理翻译过来都一模一样，就是“巴拉巴拉巴拉”。
cues.en: The macroeconomic principles all have the exact same translation, namely "Blah blah blah".

cues.zh: 证据嘛，我只提醒你一点：宏观经济学家成功预测了过去5次衰退中的9次……
cues.en: As proof I should only remind you that macroeconomists have successfully predicted 9 out of the last 5 recessions...

cues.zh: ……再给个证据，现在我们可以把字号调大一号。正如爱因斯坦所说：“一切都应尽可能简单，但不能更简单。”
cues.en: …and as further proof we can now go up one font size. As Einstein said, "Everything should be as simple as possible, if not simpler."

cues.zh: 好，回到微观经济学。
cues.en: Okay, back to microeconomics.

cues.zh: 第一条，“人们面临权衡取舍”。翻译过来就是：“做选择很糟糕。”
cues.en: The first one, "People face tradeoffs". Translation: "Choices are bad."

cues.zh: 这是个简单的三段论：权衡取舍很糟糕；每次你做选择，你都在权衡取舍；所以做选择很糟糕。
cues.en: This is a simple syllogism: Tradeoffs are bad; every time you have a choice you have a tradeoff; therefore choices are bad.

cues.zh: 如果没听懂，看第二条原理，“某种东西的成本是你为得到它所放弃的东西。”
cues.en: If you don't understand that, look at Principle #2, "The cost of something is what you give up to get it."

cues.zh: 翻译过来就是：“做选择真是太糟糕了。”
cues.en: Translation: "Choices are really bad."

cues.zh: 我给大家举个简单的例子。假设有人给你一块士力架，你估它值1美元。
cues.en: Let me just give you a simple example of this. Let's say someone offers you a Snickers bar that you value at $1.

cues.zh: 那么在这种情况下，你的经济利润就是士力架的价值减去你为得到它而放弃的成本，而后者是零……
cues.en: So your economic profit in this case is the Snickers bar minus the cost of what you give up to get it, which is nothing...

cues.zh: ……所以你的经济利润是1美元。
cues.en: ...your economic profit is $1.

cues.zh: 现在，有人让你在士力架和M&M豆之间选一个，士力架你估1美元，M&M豆你估0.70美元。
cues.en: Now, somebody offers you a choice between a Snickers bar, which you value at $1, and some M&Ms, which you value at $0.70.

cues.zh: 这时你的经济利润就是1美元减去0.70美元：只有0.30美元。
cues.en: Now your economic profit is the $1 minus the $0.70: only $0.30.

cues.zh: 你开始明白为什么选择是件坏事了。
cues.en: You begin to see why choices are bad.

cues.zh: 事实上，最糟糕的情况，是有人让你在一块士力架……和一块一模一样的士力架之间做选择。
cues.en: The worst possible situation, in fact, would be someone offering you a choice between a Snickers bar... and an identical Snickers bar.

cues.zh: 没学过经济学的人可能会觉得，这跟直接给你一块士力架没什么区别……
cues.en: Now, people who are not trained in economics might think that that's no different from being offered one Snickers bar...

cues.zh: ……但这种马虎的思维永远没法让你拿到终身教职。
cues.en: ...but that sort of sloppy thinking will never get you a tenure-track position.

cues.zh: 好，咱们简化一下：选择是坏事，非常糟糕。
cues.en: Great, let's simplify this: Choices are bad, really bad.

cues.zh: 如果你不明白为什么选择是坏事，那你大概挺蠢的。
cues.en: If you don't understand why choices are bad, you're probably stupid.

cues.zh: 下一条原则：“理性人在边际上思考。”翻译过来就是：“人是愚蠢的。”
cues.en: Next principle: "Rational people think at the margin." Translation: "People are stupid."

cues.zh: 现在，哪怕是最漫不经心的观察者、智力最平庸的人也能一眼看出，人根本不在边际上思考。
cues.en: Now, it is immediately obvious to the most casual observer with the meanest intelligence that people do not think at the margin.

cues.zh: 没人会走进杂货店说：“我要买个橙子，我要再买个橙子，我要再买个橙子。”
cues.en: Nobody goes to a grocery store and says "I'm going to buy an orange, I'm going to buy another orange, I'm going to buy another orange."

cues.zh: 但如果人不在边际上思考，而按曼昆的说法，理性人确实在边际上思考……
cues.en: But if people don't think at the margin, and if as Mankiw says rational people do think at the margin...

cues.zh: ……那我们就得出一个非常不幸的结论：人并不理性。
cues.en: ...we are led to a most unhappy conclusion: People are not rational.

cues.zh: 换句话说，人是愚蠢的。
cues.en: People, in other words, are stupid.

cues.zh: 但先别急着为人类的命运担忧。看看下一条原则：“人会对激励做出反应。”
cues.en: But don't fear for the fate of humanity yet. Take a look at the next principle: "People respond to incentives."

cues.zh: 词典上说，“激励”是个名词，意思是“促使行动的东西，同义词是‘动机’。”
cues.en: Now the dictionary says that "incentive" is a noun that means "something that influences to action, synonym 'motive'."

cues.zh: 所以曼昆在这里说的是，人会被动机所驱动……
cues.en: So what Mankiw is saying here is that people are motivated by motives...

cues.zh: ……或者说，他们会被那些促使他们行动的东西促使行动。
cues.en: ...or that they are influenced to action by things that influence them to action.

cues.zh: 你可能会觉得，这有点像在说同义反复就是同义反复的，对吧？
cues.en: Now, you might think this is a bit like saying that tautologies are tautological, right?

cues.zh: 我是说，人得蠢到什么程度，才会不被动机驱动……
cues.en: I mean, people would have to be pretty stupid to be unmotivated by motives...

cues.zh: ……或者被那些促使他们行动的东西促使不行动，对吧？
cues.en: ...or to be influenced to inaction by things that influence them to action, right?

cues.zh: 但别忘了第3条原则：“人是愚蠢的。”
cues.en: But remember Principle #3, "People are stupid."

cues.zh: 所以需要原则4来说服我们“人们没那么蠢”。
cues.en: Hence the need for Principle #4 to convince us that "People aren't that stupid."

cues.zh: 好，再简化一下，我们继续聊自由贸易，这是我们最爱的话题。
cues.en: Great, so simplifying again, let's move on to free trade, our favorite topic.

cues.zh: 原则5，“贸易能让每个人都变得更好”。翻译过来就是：“贸易能让每个人都变得更糟。”
cues.en: Principle #5, "Trade can make everyone better off". Translation: "Trade can make everyone worse off."

cues.zh: 关于这个事实，我有一个会让你大开眼界的证明。来了：
cues.en: I have a proof that will blow your mind of this fact. Here we go:

cues.zh: 比较下面两句话。一句是“贸易能让每个人都变得更好”，另一句是“贸易会让每个人都变得更好”。
cues.en: Compare the following two statements. One is "Trade can make everyone better off", the other is "Trade will make everyone better off".

cues.zh: 如果让你在这两者之间选，那毫无悬念，对吧？第二句更好。但曼昆用的是第一句。
cues.en: If you had to choose between those it's no contest, right? Claim #2 is better. But Mankiw uses Claim #1.

cues.zh: 那就只有一种解释：第二句肯定是错的。
cues.en: And there's only one explanation: Claim #2 has to be wrong.

cues.zh: 换句话说，贸易能让一些人变得更糟，而从这儿到“贸易能让每个人都变得更糟”也就一步之遥。
cues.en: In other words, trade can make some people worse off, and it's just a hop, skip, and a jump from there to "Trade can make everyone worse off."

cues.zh: 有些人显然不喜欢这个解构性证明，或者说破坏性证明，他们想要一个构造性证明……
cues.en: Some people apparently didn't like this deconstructive proof, or destructive proof, they wanted a constructive proof...

cues.zh: ……所以我加了这个脚注，把细节写进去。
cues.en: ...so I added this footnote with the details.

cues.zh: 现在注意最后这两句，“政府是愚蠢的”和“政府没那么愚蠢”……
cues.en: Now notice the final two here, "Governments are stupid" and "Governments aren't that stupid"...

cues.zh: ……直接由原则#5及其翻译推出。
cues.en: ...follow immediately from Principle #5 and its translation.

cues.zh: 如果贸易能让每个人都变得更好，那我们到底要政府干什么？
cues.en: If trade can make everyone better off, what the heck do we need government for?

cues.zh: 但如果贸易会让每个人都变得更糟，那我们最好有个政府来阻止人们交易。
cues.en: But if trade can make everyone worse off, we better have a government around to stop people from trading.

cues.zh: 这些就是经济学原理的翻译版。
cues.en: Here are the principles of economics, translated.

cues.zh: 这是我的网站，standupeconomist.com。感谢各位的时间。
cues.en: And there is my website, standupeconomist.com. Thank you for your time.
